candidates.name: WFH Research SWAA data portal
candidates.what_it_holds: Direct Excel and JSON downloads of the Survey of Working Arrangements and Attitudes (SWAA), Bloom/Davis/Barrero's monthly US survey on work-from-home share, days-WFH, and related attitudes since May 2020; also an application process for anonymized respondent-level microdata. No GitHub mirror found — data lives on the project's own site, not a repo.
candidates.why_useful: This IS the WFH Research SWAA dataset named in gap 16 (remote-work / long-stay demand proxy for ABNB's long-stay and 'live anywhere' nights mix). Point-in-time monthly releases could be vintage-tracked.
candidates.size_hint: Excel/JSON summary tables; microdata via application
candidates.license: unclear — check site terms before quoting

candidates.name: Digital-Nomad-Research
candidates.what_it_holds: Data/Processed/DigitalNomadDataset.xlsx with two linked worksheets: a 190-country macro/tourism panel (2,464 country-year observations: GDP, unemployment, inflation, FX, internet penetration, tourism arrivals/expenditure/employment/GDP share, sourced from World Bank + UN Tourism) and a 33-jurisdiction human-verified digital-nomad-visa policy audit with field-level provenance (source URLs, access dates, raw values). MIT-licensed code, 94 commits, active.
candidates.why_useful: Directly fills gap 16 (digital-nomad visa dataset) with a genuine policy panel plus a much broader 190-country tourism/macro panel that could substitute or cross-check for LatAm/APAC travel-volume gaps (gap 7).
candidates.time_coverage: multi-year panel (years not fully specified in README summary)
candidates.size_hint: one xlsx, 2,464 rows in macro panel + 33 policy records
candidates.license: MIT (code); third-party data retains original licence

candidates.name: global-emigration-dataset
candidates.what_it_holds: 9 committed CSVs: easiest-countries-2026.csv, digital-nomad-visas-2026.csv (income requirements per programme), visa-processing-times-2026.csv, immigration-pathways-by-category-2026.csv, visa-thresholds-global-2026.csv, cost-of-living-global-2026.csv, salary-by-profession-global-2026.csv, quality-of-life-global-2026.csv, data-dictionary.csv. Covers 190+ countries, 2,500+ visa/residency pathways, sourced from a third-party site (WhereToEmigrate.io), July 2026 snapshot, CC BY 4.0, only 2 commits.
candidates.why_useful: Broad digital-nomad-visa and cost-of-living cross-country dataset (gap 16); the cost-of-living-global-2026.csv could proxy destination attractiveness/affordability shifts relevant to nights mix, though provenance (a single third-party site scrape) and only 2 commits warrant caution.
candidates.time_coverage: single July 2026 snapshot, claimed quarterly refresh

candidates.name: open-nomad-visa-data
candidates.what_it_holds: visa-data.json + schema.json covering 11 countries' digital-nomad/remote-work visas: income thresholds, processing times, dependant rules, tax notes, path-to-residency flags, with a meta.lastUpdated field per record. CC-BY-4.0 data, MIT code examples.
candidates.why_useful: Small but structured, machine-readable digital-nomad-visa dataset for gap 16; thinner than the two above (only 11 countries) but has an explicit last-updated field useful for point-in-time tracking of visa rule changes.
candidates.time_coverage: current snapshot with per-record lastUpdated field

candidates.name: global-nomad-atlas
candidates.what_it_holds: Per search-result description only (not independently verified): scoring across 80 cities in 40 countries on 12 evaluation dimensions plus 60 community maps for digital-nomad location research. Not fetched directly — flag for follow-up verification before citing.
candidates.why_useful: If real, a city-level nomad-friendliness/cost index (gap 16/20 adjacent) broader than Nomad List's own paywalled data.

candidates.name: nomadlistscraper
candidates.what_it_holds: Python scraper + Jupyter notebook (Nomadlist-Scraper.ipynb) plus a /data directory for output, built explicitly 'to understand the movements of digital nomads' from nomadlist.com. GitHub Actions workflow for automation. 2 commits, 1 star — minimal activity, no license stated.
candidates.why_useful: A working acquisition method for Nomad List city-level nomad population/movement data (gap 16) — a non-Airbnb site scraper, in scope per CONTEXT.md rules (catalogue as method, do not run).

candidates.name: nomadlist (CRAN mirror)
candidates.what_it_holds: Read-only GitHub mirror of an R package (from CRAN) providing an interface to the Nomad List API — programmatic R client for city cost/quality-of-life metrics Nomad List tracks. Single commit, archival mirror only, no committed data.
candidates.why_useful: A ready-made API client for Nomad List (gap 16), lower engineering lift than a scraper if the underlying API still responds.
candidates.license: unspecified on mirror; check original CRAN package

candidates.name: gypsylist
candidates.what_it_holds: Python/Selenium scraper (gypsylist.py) for nomadlist.com, pulling city ratings across cost, internet quality, safety, and overall suitability categories via user-supplied nomadlist.com filter URLs. GPL-3.0, 11 stars, 5 forks, 3 commits, no committed output data.
candidates.why_useful: Another working Nomad List acquisition method (gap 16), somewhat more established (11 stars) than nomadlistscraper.

candidates.name: Justlanded
candidates.what_it_holds: Python/Playwright scraper targeting Blueground's listing API (despite the repo description also naming Furnished Finder, only Blueground is implemented), with committed sample Excel outputs (listings.xlsx, sf-listings.xlsx) containing beds/baths/sqft/price-per-month/move-in/min-stay/address/city/state/lat/lon/source/link columns. Built as an MIT-course (15.573) group project; 10 commits.
candidates.why_useful: A working, verified acquisition method plus sample committed data for Blueground furnished/corporate-housing pricing — directly on-theme (coliving/corporate housing) and a possible template for pulling comparable mid-term-rental pricing to compare against ABNB long-stay ADR.
candidates.geography: at least San Francisco (sf-listings.xlsx); scraper is general
candidates.size_hint: two small Excel sample files + scraper code
candidates.last_activity: 10 commits, course project, dated activity unclear

candidates.name: furnished-finder-scraper (Apify actor)
candidates.what_it_holds: An Apify-actor-wrapped scraper for Furnished Finder rental listings (travel-nurse-oriented mid-term/furnished housing marketplace). No committed data, code only, packaged for Apify's cloud-run platform. Related sibling repos from the same and other accounts: furnished-finder-fast, furnished-finder-rental-listings-scraper (AbsoluteAnchor), furnished-finder-hosts (HumbleIgnite), and a browser extension scraper (scaprisecca/furnished-finder-scraper-extension).
candidates.why_useful: A ready acquisition method for Furnished Finder mid-term-rental listing prices/host counts — the theme's named platform — though it is a scraper of a non-Airbnb site (in scope as 'method', per CONTEXT.md, left unrun).

candidates.name: zeus (API Evangelist profile)
candidates.what_it_holds: Kin Lane's 'API Evangelist' independent third-party documentation profile of Zeus Living's (the now-defunct furnished/corporate-housing rental startup) API surface — describes the company and its API design, not a data dump or working client. No committed data, 0 stars.
candidates.why_useful: Marginal: only documents that Zeus Living had an API and describes it; no data or working code to pull anything, and Zeus Living itself is defunct. Useful only as a pointer if someone later needs to understand what Zeus's API exposed.

notes: This session's WebSearch tool was exhausted (200/200) before any query for this theme ran (shared session-wide budget consumed by other concurrent scouts), and github.com/search's normal web UI plus DuckDuckGo HTML search were both blocked (429 rate limit / CAPTCHA respectively). Bing via WebFetch loaded but the summarizing sub-model did not reliably honor the site:github.com filter, returning generic results instead. Pivoted to fetching the public GitHub REST API (api.github.com/search/repositories) via WebFetch, which worked for ~7 queries before hitting GitHub's unauthenticated 60-req/hour search rate limit (403s thereafter) — could not run every planned query (corporate housing scraper, mid-term rental dataset, remote work index cities, remote work visa tracker all 403'd before returning). Landing (the corporate-housing company) and Blueground's own name turned up nothing beyond the Justlanded student scraper; no genuine Landing/Blueground open dataset found. WFH Research's SWAA data has no GitHub mirror — it is a direct-download portal, recorded as pointer_to_external_host and rated high since it is the exact named target in gap 16. Two of the digital-nomad-visa repos (genesysc/open-nomad-visa-data, 0brien18/global-emigration-dataset) read as likely AI-assembled or thin scrapes of a single third-party site (WhereToEmigrate.io) rather than primary-sourced research — flagged at low/medium potential accordingly, not excluded outright since the files are real and committed. Roloria/global-nomad-atlas was found only in search-result metadata and NOT independently verified by fetching the repo page — flag for a follow-up scout to confirm before citing. Recommend a future pass with a fresh WebSearch budget and/or an authenticated GitHub token to properly cover: Landing.com corporate housing, Sonder/Vacasa GitHub mirrors (not this theme but same rate-limit problem likely recurs), and a second attempt at 'SWAA' / 'work from home survey' phrasing variants which returned zero hits here.
